title: DomainFit architecture and confidence guidance
purpose: Teach architecture selection and calibrated uncertainty without treating synthetic scores as facts.

use_when: the task is broad and low risk
generic model capabilities and prompting are sufficient
no stable specialist behavior has been demonstrated
avoid_when: current evidence, private data, controlled actions, or stable specialist behavior is required

use_when: terminology, response structure, decision patterns, or escalation behavior must remain stable
representative approved examples and stable source material are available
avoid_when: the primary need is current facts, live data, permissions, calculations, or actions

use_when: answers require exact approved evidence or citations
avoid_when: the primary requirement is stable behavior or an external action

use_when: live or private data is required
the system performs actions, calculations, permission checks, or deterministic validation
avoid_when: a model response alone can safely satisfy the requirement

use_when: stable specialist behavior must be combined with current evidence or controlled tools
high-impact workflows need validation or human approval across multiple system layers
avoid_when: one simpler architecture satisfies every material requirement

confidence_calibration.principle: Confidence describes the strength of the recommendation given the supplied evidence; it is not a memorized property of a scenario.
higher_confidence_when: requirements clearly map to documented architecture rules
source ownership, freshness, behavior targets, and risk boundaries are explicit
representative examples and measurable success criteria are available
lower_confidence_when: document authority, freshness, or coverage is unknown
tool permissions, risk ownership, or success criteria are missing
required_behavior: identify the missing evidence that would change the recommendation
never present an arbitrary numeric score as an observed fact

responsibility_boundaries.tools: live or private data, calculations, permissions, and actions
responsibility_boundaries.deterministic_logic: authorization, schemas, hard rules, idempotency, and approval gates
responsibility_boundaries.human_review: material decisions, unresolved ambiguity, and accountable approval

benchmark_guidance: test application of the framework to new scenarios rather than recall of document fields
include normal, boundary, conflicting, insufficient-information, and high-risk cases
keep a held-out evaluation set separate from alignment material
score required reasoning points and safety boundaries without rewarding verbosity
